t: A Genoese seaman who had traded from the British Isles to the Guinea coast, Columbus won the backing of Ferdinand and Isabella in 1492 for a westward route to Asia built on a badly underestimated size of the Earth.

His landfall in the Bahamas on 12 October 1492 and three later voyages opened the Caribbean and the coasts of South and Central America to Spain, though he never clearly renounced his belief that he had reached the Far East.

As governor of Hispaniola he waged war on the Taíno, imposed tribute and the encomienda and shipped enslaved people to Spain; accused of tyranny, he was arrested in 1500, and historians still dispute how far the depopulation that followed was his doing.
dyk: Stranded on Jamaica in 1504, Columbus kept the island's inhabitants supplying his men by predicting the lunar eclipse of 29 February, using Abraham Zacuto's astronomical charts.
ev: Born in the Republic of Genoa to Domenico Colombo, a wool weaver, and Susanna Fontanarossa
Shipwrecked off Lagos, Portugal, after his Genoese trading fleet is attacked, and settles in Lisbon
Agrees the Capitulations of Santa Fe with Ferdinand and Isabella in April, sails from Palos in August and reaches Guanahani in the Bahamas in October
Returns to a hero's welcome with captured Taínos, then leaves Cádiz with 17 ships and nearly 1,500 men to found colonies
Rounds up about 1,500 Arawaks in a slave raid on Hispaniola and ships about 500 to Spain, about two hundred of whom die on the way
On his third voyage sends boats ashore on the Paria Peninsula, the first recorded European landing on the mainland of South America
Arrested by Francisco de Bobadilla after charges of tyranny and brutality, and sent back to Spain in chains
Dies in Valladolid while still pressing the Crown for the privileges promised him in 1492

f.born: Between 25 August and 31 October 1451 in the Republic of Genoa, by scholarly consensus; son of Domenico Colombo, a wool weaver, and Susanna Fontanarossa
f.died: 20 May 1506 in Valladolid, aged 54, after years of illness then thought to be gout, which some modern commentators suspect was reactive arthritis
f.role: Merchant seaman and business agent (from 1473); Admiral of the Ocean Sea, Viceroy and Governor of the lands he claimed for Castile under the Capitulations of Santa Fe (1492); removed from his posts in 1500
f.known: the first voyage of 1492 and the landfall at Guanahani; four voyages across the Atlantic (1492–1504); naming the inhabitants indios; the encomienda and slave raids on Hispaniola; his arrest by Francisco de Bobadilla in 1500; the Columbian exchange named after him; the pleitos colombinos
